draft_mizo_meaning: Fing taka, ngaihtuahna nei ngei ngeiin thil ti a ni.
draft_example: Kawng kan i tum chuan remchang takin en fel rawh.

issue: “suangtuahna” usually means imagination.
draft_mizo_meaning: Thil chi hrang hrang ngaihtuah taka thlir theihna
draft_example: Kan pi leh pu suangtuahna hi kan la zir tel ang a ni.

issue: To steal is “ru”; “sut” usually means to untie / pull out. Check it.
draft_mizo_meaning: Mi thil mahni ta lo lakin lo hawn dan.
draft_example: Sut hi Mizoten an ngaih pawimawh lohzia sawi a ni.

issue: “taihmâk” means hardworking / diligent; patience is “dawhtheihna”.
draft_mizo_meaning: Tuarna leh hah nasa lai pawh a nghing thei mizia.
draft_example: Taihmâk hi mi tin nei tur a ni.

issue: “taihmâkna” means diligence / hard work; patience is “dawhtheihna”.
draft_mizo_meaning: Harsatna hmaah chhelh lova ngun taka nghah dan.
draft_example: Taihmâkna neiin a zirna a zo.

issue: “taimakna” means diligence / hard work; patience is “dawhtheihna”.
draft_mizo_meaning: Harsatna hmachhawn pawhin beidawng lovin mahni tumna zawm reng tih hriat theihna.
draft_example: Zirlai chak tak an nih hi an taimakna avanga hlawhtlinna a ni.

issue: “ṭhenawm” is a neighbour (word.thenawm-2); check “companion”.
draft_mizo_meaning: Kalpui tawnna mi, thawh tawnna mi.
draft_example: Khualzin an chuan thenawm an neih a ngai.

issue: “ṭhenawm” means neighbour; check that “ṭhenawmpa” means uncle.
draft_mizo_meaning: Pa emaw nu unau pa
draft_example: Ka thenawmpa chu ka in bul ah a cheng.

issue: “ṭhenawmte” means the neighbours; check “the needy”.
draft_mizo_meaning: Tanpui a mamawh mi te
draft_example: Thenawmte kan ṭanpui a ngai.

issue: “thluak” is the brain; the head is “lu” (word.lu).
draft_mizo_meaning: Taksa chunglam ber, rilru leh ngaihtuahna a chinna.
draft_example: Thluak hi taksa peng pawimawh tak a ni.

issue: “darh” means to spread / scatter, so “tidarh” is to spread something out, not to strengthen.
draft_mizo_meaning: Nghak thei zawk leh chak zawka siam dan.
draft_example: Tawngtaina chuan rilru min tidarh ṭhin.

issue: “tihpalh” means to do something by mistake, not specifically to bump into.
draft_mizo_meaning: Ngaihtuah lovin mi emaw thil emaw khoih dan
draft_example: Kalkawngah chuan mi ka tihpalh chuan ka ngaidam ṭhin.

issue: “tinreng” means of every kind / all sorts, not always.
draft_mizo_meaning: A chatuan zêl, hun tinah awm reng dan.
draft_example: Kan pa min chhâwrtîr tinreng a duh.

issue: “vak” usually means to roam / walk about; to fly is “thlawk”.
draft_mizo_meaning: Sava emaw khuai emaw chuan thla hmangin chung lamah a kal chhuahna a ni.
draft_example: Vahai chu tlang chunga chuan a vak chhoh zel a.

issue: “vakvai” usually means a wanderer / vagrant; an orphan is “fahrah” or “chhawmdawl”.
draft_mizo_meaning: Nu leh pa hlum tawh, en chhungkuate awm lo hi a ni.
draft_example: Vakvai nau chu mi zawngin an khawngaih.

issue: “vir” usually means to spin / whirl; to shout is “au”.
draft_mizo_meaning: Aw ngaihnawm taka au chhuah a ni.
draft_example: A hlau avangin a vir chhuak a.

issue: “zaidam” usually means gentle / meek, the opposite of conceited.
draft_mizo_meaning: Zaidam tih hi mahni chungchang inchhinbawrh taka i ngaih dan a ni.
draft_example: Zaidam mi chu mi dangin an duh ngai lo.

issue: “zâl” usually means to lie down; check “calm”.
draft_mizo_meaning: Thli leh tuipui buai lo, muang taka awm dan
draft_example: Tuipui a zal hunah chuan lawngte an kal tha zawk ṭhin.

issue: A nest is “bu” (sava bu); check “zâmna”.
draft_mizo_meaning: Zâmna chu sava chenna leh mahni siam hmun a ni.
draft_example: Sava chuan thingah zâmna a siam.

issue: “zilh” means to advise / warn; to bathe someone is “bual”.
draft_mizo_meaning: Tui hmangin taksa siangsak tihna.
draft_example: Nau tê chu a nu chuan a zilh thin.

issue: The Mizo meaning says it catches crabs (chakai manna), the English says fish.
draft_english_meaning: woven bamboo trap for catching crabs
draft_mizo_meaning: Chakai manna chi, hnâng tah puma, patling malpui tia vêl.
draft_example: Aiâwt chhungah chuan chakai duh zawng an dah a.

issue: The English is still marked “species uncertain”.
draft_mizo_meaning: Rim ṭha tak nei par chi pakhat, khawvar chuan a par a inphel thin.
draft_example: Kan huan ah Artukkhuan par a par a, a rim chu kan hnai vek thin.

issue: The Mizo meaning (“something thought essential”) does not match the English (“a hidden danger that may flare up”).
draft_english_meaning: "like fire smouldering under ash" — a hidden danger that may flare up
draft_mizo_meaning: Tel ngei ngei tura ngaih, tel lo thei lo, pawimawh sawina.
draft_example: Sikul naupang tan chuan pen hi a serh zinga a mei ang mai a ni.

issue: The literal English (“bitten by one's own snake”) does not match the Mizo words, which have no word for snake.
draft_english_meaning: "bitten by one's own snake" — undone by one's own trick
draft_mizo_meaning: Mahni tih hmasa lehin mahni tan a harsa a chhuahsan chi.
draft_example: A tlawm zâwkah a tang leh si a, a vawtuin êk a cheh tih ang mai a ni.

issue: “hma tiang” means forwards / ahead.
draft_mizo_meaning: "-tiang" tawi hmang, kawng emaw dan sawina a ni.
draft_example: Hmatiang hian kal ang che, chumi hnuah i lo pan thei ang.

issue: “hmusit” / “hmuhsit” means to despise (word.hmuhsit); a trap is “thang” or “hnâng”.
draft_mizo_meaning: Ram sa man nan siam thil.
draft_example: Pasaltha chuan sa man nan hmusit an siam ṭhin.

issue: Far is “hla” (word.hla); check “khâr”.
draft_mizo_meaning: A hnai lo va, hmun rei takah awm a ni.
draft_example: Ka pi in chu kan in atangin a khâr hle a.

issue: “tawlailir” usually means a cart / wheeled vehicle; check “swing / seesaw”.
draft_mizo_meaning: Tawlailir chu insawi nan hman puitling, tui chunga khan pahnih insawi thei chi a ni.
draft_example: Naupang te chuan tawlailirah an insawi.
